identity.title: Statistical Query Hardness of Multiclass Linear Classification with Random Classification Noise

problem.claim: Study multiclass linear classification under distribution-free PAC learning with known random classification noise, seeking a hypothesis with small 0-1 error.

gap.claim: Although the two-label case has polynomial-time algorithms achieving optimal error, little is known about complexity for three labels.

contributions.claim: Proves super-polynomial statistical query lower bounds for multiclass linear classification with random classification noise.
Establishes lower bounds under distinct label-count and noise-separation regimes, including weaker learning objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that the complexity changes drastically at three or more labels and present corresponding super-polynomial SQ lower bounds.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, with three labels and constant separation, any SQ algorithm achieving optimal error has super-polynomial complexity.

The authors report that, for more labels and smaller separation, achieving any constant-factor approximation to optimal loss—or even beating the trivial hypothesis—has a super-polynomial SQ lower bound.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines multiclass linear classification in the distribution-free PAC model with random classification noise generated through a known noise matrix.
Frames learning as computing a hypothesis with small 0-1 error.
Contrasts the known two-label result with limited understanding of the three-label case.
Reports super-polynomial SQ lower bounds for optimal-error learning with three labels, and for weaker goals with more labels and smaller separation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states lower bounds separately by number of labels, noise separation, and target guarantee, including the weaker benchmark of beating the trivial hypothesis.

lessons.interpretation: Complexity claims become more informative when their parameter regime and success criterion are stated together.
lessons.application: When presenting a hardness result, explicitly tabulate how task size, noise separation, and approximation target affect the claim.
lessons.exception: This framing is less useful when the result is uniform across parameters or the abstract lacks meaningful regime distinctions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact SQ complexity lower-bound exponents, dimension dependence, or formal assumptions beyond the stated regimes.
It does not identify the trivial hypothesis or quantify the optimal loss and separation thresholds.
